epics.title: Public API for External AI Agents
epics.jtbd: When an external AI agent operates on behalf of a user, I want it to securely read documentation, place service orders, and send direct messages, so that the user can seamlessly hire me or contact me through their personal assistant.
epics.sixSigmaMetric: API uptime and successful request parsing rate
epics.tocConstraintRef: Rate limiting and abuse prevention processing
requirements: R1: The system must serve public, machine-readable API documentation (e.g., OpenAPI schema, llms.txt) detailing the service order and direct message endpoints.
R2: The system must provide a public API endpoint for external AI agents to place service orders (MVP, audit, automation) on behalf of users.
R3: The system must provide a public API endpoint for external AI agents to send direct messages to the author on behalf of users.
R4: The system must validate and store the submitted orders and messages reliably in a structured data schema.
R5: The system must automatically and immediately acknowledge the receipt of any service order or direct message to the submitting agent, detailing what was received and next steps.
R6: The system must immediately notify the author (e.g., via email or internal alert) when a new service order or direct message is successfully received and stored.
R7: The system must handle failed validation (e.g., missing required fields, rate limits exceeded) gracefully by returning descriptive error codes (e.g., HTTP 400, 429) to the submitting agent.

slices.title: Data schema for AI orders and messages
slices.jtbd: When implementing data storage for this epic, I want to define the relational schema for AI-originated service orders and messages, so that incoming API requests can be durably persisted.
slices.acceptanceCriteria:
Given a service order submission, When persisted, Then the database stores the user details, service type, and timestamp.
Given a direct message submission, When persisted, Then the database stores the sender details, content, and timestamp.
slices.sixSigmaMetric: Zero schema validation errors on insertion

slices.title: AI Agent API Endpoints and Documentation
slices.jtbd: When implementing the backend for this epic, I want to expose machine-readable documentation and secure endpoints for orders and messages, so that AI agents can discover and interact with the service.
slices.acceptanceCriteria:
Given an AI agent request for documentation, When accessing the root or llms.txt, Then the system returns machine-readable API specifications.
Given a valid service order or direct message payload, When submitted, Then the system stores the payload and returns an immediate automated acknowledgement of receipt.
Given an invalid request payload or excessive rate, When submitted, Then the system rejects it and returns a descriptive error code.
slices.tocConstraintRef: API request validation and rate limiting

slices.title: Author Notification for AI Submissions
slices.jtbd: When implementing notifications for this epic, I want to ensure the author is proactively informed of new incoming requests, so that they can promptly read and respond to them.
slices.acceptanceCriteria:
Given a successfully stored service order or message, When the transaction commits, Then an email or system notification is dispatched to the author.
Given a notification dispatch, When sent, Then it includes the sender's details and the content of the request.

slices.title: QA for AI Agent API Flows
slices.jtbd: When verifying this epic, I want to test the full lifecycle of an AI agent interaction, so that I am confident the endpoints correctly process requests, store data, notify the author, and return acknowledgements.
slices.acceptanceCriteria:
Given the testing environment, When an integration test simulates an AI agent discovering endpoints and submitting an order, Then the test verifies the documentation is returned, the order is stored, the author is notified, and an acknowledgement is sent.
Given the acceptance environment, When the database is pre-populated with actual service categories from the brief (MVP, audit, automation), Then the end-to-end API correctly accepts orders against those realistic categories.
slices.sixSigmaMetric: 100% test coverage of agent API paths

epics.title: Platform Telemetry and Measurement
epics.jtbd: When operating the site, I want to measure visitor engagement with my content and external links, so that I know if the site successfully drives interest in my work.
epics.sixSigmaMetric: 100% telemetry capture rate for successful AI API events
requirements: R1: The system must track metrics derived via Goal-Question-Metric alignment: Goal is to enable automated lead generation via external AI agents.
R2: The system must instrument metrics to answer the questions 'Are external AIs successfully placing service orders?' and 'Are they sending direct messages?' by counting successful API submissions.
R3: A telemetry metric must answer none other than the stated questions, avoiding unnecessary event tracking.

slices.title: Telemetry for AI Agent Interactions
slices.jtbd: When implementing measurement for this epic, I want to add telemetry to the AI agent endpoints, so that the success rate and volume of automated leads can be tracked.
slices.acceptanceCriteria:
Given an AI agent successfully submitting a service order or message, When the transaction completes, Then a metric counter is incremented for the specific interaction type.
Given a telemetry dashboard or endpoint, When queried, Then it reports the total number of AI-originated orders and messages.

slices.title: QA for AI Agent Telemetry
slices.jtbd: When verifying telemetry for this epic, I want to ensure the API accurately records metrics for orders and messages, so that business insights are reliable.
slices.acceptanceCriteria:
Given a suite of integration tests, When valid API interactions occur, Then the test asserts that the correct metric counters are incremented.
Given a failed or rejected API interaction, When processed, Then the success metric counters are not incremented.

epics.title: Data Subject Rights and GDPR Compliance
epics.jtbd: When a user whose personal data was submitted by an AI agent requests access or deletion, I want to be able to export or erase their data within the statutory deadline, so that the system complies with privacy regulations.
epics.sixSigmaMetric: Zero regulatory compliance breaches for data requests
requirements: R1: The system must allow exporting a data subject's submitted personal data upon request within statutory deadlines.
R2: The system must allow erasing a data subject's submitted personal data upon request, completely removing it from the database.

slices.title: Data Export and Erasure Mechanisms
slices.jtbd: When implementing compliance for this epic, I want to create mechanisms to extract and permanently delete user data submitted by AI agents, so that subject rights requests can be fulfilled.
slices.acceptanceCriteria:
Given a valid request for data export, When processed, Then the system returns all personal data (orders and messages) associated with the specified user.
Given a valid request for erasure, When processed, Then the system permanently deletes all personal data associated with the specified user.
slices.tocConstraintRef: Database query generation for cross-table deletion
slices.sixSigmaMetric: 100% success rate for data deletion execution

slices.title: QA for Data Subject Rights Mechanisms
slices.jtbd: When verifying compliance mechanisms for this epic, I want to ensure export and erasure accurately process all linked personal data, so that legal obligations are met without data leakage.
slices.acceptanceCriteria:
Given a test user with populated data, When the export mechanism is invoked, Then the output contains exactly the test user's data and no one else's.
Given a test user with populated data, When the erasure mechanism is invoked, Then subsequent queries confirm no remaining data is linked to that user.

epics.title: Data Protection and Recovery
epics.jtbd: When the database experiences a failure, I want to be able to restore the system state from a backup, so that I do not lose my published content.
requirements: R1: The system must routinely backup database contents, including AI agent submitted service orders and direct messages.
R2: The system must verify the backup can be successfully restored into a functional instance.

slices.title: Backup Schedule and Retention
slices.jtbd: When configuring infrastructure for this epic, I want to automate daily database backups, so that disaster recovery is possible.
slices.acceptanceCriteria:
Given a running system, When the scheduled time is reached, Then a complete database backup is generated and stored securely.
Given a set of historical backups, When older than the retention policy, Then they are automatically purged.

slices.title: Restore Verification Testing
slices.jtbd: When verifying disaster recovery for this epic, I want to test the restore process with real data, so that I am confident the backups are actually functional.
slices.acceptanceCriteria:
Given a database backup containing service orders and messages, When the restore process is initiated on a fresh instance, Then the system successfully starts and the restored data is accessible.
Given a restored database, When validation queries run, Then no data loss or corruption is detected compared to the backup snapshot.
slices.sixSigmaMetric: 100% test coverage of the restoration runbook
